title: CVE-2026-86415: auto client cert connection reuse mixup
excerpt:
Howdy,

libcurl's connection-cache matcher never checks `auto_client_cert`, so a cached, already-authenticated Schannel connection can be handed to a transfer that just got redirected to a different origin, even though the code explicitly computed `auto_client_cert = FALSE` for that transfer to prevent exactly this.

## The bug

`Curl_ssl_easy_config_complete()` recomputes the effective SSL config for every request, including a request that is the result of following a `Location:` redirect. Part of that is deciding whether the automatically-selected client certificate applies:

```c
// lib/vtls/vtls_config.c:236-238
sslc->auto_client_cert = Curl_peer_equal(origin, initial_origin) &&
                         !!(options & CURLSSLOPT_AUTO_CLIENT_CERT);
```

`initial_origin` is the origin of the very first URL of the `curl_easy_perform()`, set once and kept for the whole redirect chain. So the moment a redirect takes the transfer to a different host, `auto_client_cert` is correctly forced to `FALSE` — the client shouldn't auto-present a certificate to a host it wasn't explicitly pointed at.

The problem is that this flag lives in `struct ssl_config_data`, not in `struct ssl_primary_config`:

```c
// lib/vtls/vtls_config.h:74-75
BIT(auto_client_cert);   /* automatically locate and use a client
                            certificate for authentication (Schannel) */
```

and connections in the pool only ever retain the primary struct:

```c
// lib/urldata.h:322
struct ssl_primary_config ssl_config;
```

Connection reuse is decided by `match_ssl_primary_config()`, which takes two `ssl_primary_config *` and therefore has no way to see `auto_client_cert` even in principle:

```c
// lib/vtls/vtls_config.c:136-146
static bool match_ssl_primary_config(struct Curl_easy *data,
                                     struct ssl_primary_config *c1,
                                     struct ssl_primary_config *c2)
{
  (void)data;
  if((c1->version == c2->version) &&
     (c1->version_max == c2->version_max) &&
     (c1->ssl_options == c2->ssl_options) &&
     (c1->native_ca_store == c2->native_ca_store) &&
     (c1->verifypeer == c2->verifypeer) &&
     (c1->verifyhost == c2->verifyhost) &&
```

`ssl_options` (the raw `CURLOPT_SSL_OPTIONS` bitmask, including the `CURLSSLOPT_AUTO_CLIENT_CERT` bit) is identical on every request from the same easy handle, so it always matches. T
explain: The code supports the reported flaw. A maintainer should review its impact and decide what to do next.
summary: libcurl's connection cache reuses a Schannel connection authenticated with a client certificate to a different origin after a redirect, bypassing the per-request auto_client_cert=FALSE check.

claims.text: The connection cache matcher never checks the per-request auto_client_cert flag, allowing reuse of a cached connection that was established with auto_client_cert=TRUE for a request that should have auto_client_cert=FALSE.
claims.reasoning: The code confirms auto_client_cert is derived per-request (line 236-238) but connection matching only uses ssl_primary_config which lacks this field. The raw ssl_options bitmask is compared but it doesn't capture the per-origin derivation.

claims.text: A redirect from an attacker-controlled host causes a request to reuse an existing cached connection to a different host that was established with client certificate authentication.
claims.reasoning: A redirect changes origin but not initial_origin, so auto_client_cert becomes FALSE for the redirected request. However, the connection matcher doesn't check this flag, so a cached connection established with auto_client_cert=TRUE (for initial_origin) can be reused.

claims.text: The client certificate is sent to the original host (B) instead of the redirect target (A), allowing the attacker to obtain resources or actions intended for the authenticated host.
claims.reasoning: When a cached connection is reused, no new handshake occurs, so the schannel flags that would suppress client cert presentation are never evaluated. The attacker-controlled redirect target (A) causes reuse of B's authenticated session, letting A steer authenticated requests to B.

claims.text: Create a redirect chain that leads to a host B for which a cached Schannel connection with auto_client_cert=TRUE exists, then follow the redirect with a client that has CURLSSLOPT_AUTO_CLIENT_CERT set; the cached connection is reused without a new handshake.
claims.reasoning: The reproduction steps follow directly from the code: establish a connection to B with auto_client_cert=TRUE (B == initial_origin), then have A redirect to B. The redirected request computes auto_client_cert=FALSE but the matcher ignores it, reusing B's authenticated connection.

external_sources.for: The match_ssl_primary_config() function compares only struct ssl_primary_config fields and therefore cannot differentiate connections based on auto_client_cert.

key_reasons: auto_client_cert is computed per-request based on origin vs initial_origin (vtls_config.c:236-238) to prevent presenting client certs to redirected hosts
Connection cache matcher (match_ssl_primary_config) only compares ssl_primary_config fields, which excludes auto_client_cert (vtls_config.c:136-169, vtls_config.h:62-79, urldata.h:322)

A redirect from attacker-controlled host A to host B causes reuse of B's cached authenticated connection because the matcher doesn't see that auto_client_cert should be FALSE for the redirected request
Schannel uses auto_client_cert at handshake time (schannel.c:783-786, 981) but connection reuse bypasses handshake entirely
The flaw was introduced by commit d69bfad3fa3daf5e72331f6870667607828d5891 which added the per-origin check but didn't update the matcher, and persists at master (e26f6e408a80)
reply: Thank you for the detailed report. The code confirms the flaw: `auto_client_cert` is correctly derived per-request to block client certs on redirects (vtls_config.c:236-238), but `match_ssl_primary_config()` only compares `ssl_primary_config` fields (vtls_config.c:136-169), which lacks this flag. A cached Schannel connection established with `auto_client_cert=TRUE` can be reused for a redirected request where it should be `FALSE`, bypassing the handshake where Schannel would suppress the cert (schannel.c:783-786, 981). This is a valid security issue on Windows/Schannel with `CURLSSLOPT_AUTO_CLIENT_CERT`.
